caption:
Why are we so unhealthy? Pt. 1

Also there is simply not enough board to answer that question, add what I missed in the comments

#fyp #health #microplastic #food #pharma
audio_track_actual: Spoken monologue (creator voiceover), no music bed.
video_overlay_text_observed: Cover card: 'Why are we so unhealthy pt 1' over a dense handwritten whiteboard of the same argument. The whiteboard text mirrors the spoken monologue.
audio_content_summary: A single-take 'rant board' survey of why Americans are unhealthy, tracing a century of industry incentives: the 1910 Flexner Report and Rockefeller-funded reshaping of medical education toward pharmacology; the 1960s birth-control pill as recurring revenue; the 1964 Surgeon General smoking report and tobacco firms' 1980s move into food (Nabisco, General Foods, Kraft); tobacco flavor science applied to ultra-processed food; PDUFA industry funding of the FDA; Purdue/Sackler OxyContin; Nestle formula and AAP funding conflicts; the 1992 food pyramid; the GRAS 'prove-it-unsafe' loophole vs the EU precautionary standard; and the chronic-disease share of US health spending.
implied_frame: The reel's spine is a real thesis — that the US medical and food systems are shaped by industry profit incentives — built from a mix of verifiable primary facts and contested causal glue. Group A (recorded): the Flexner Report and the medical-school closures it drove; tobacco companies' 1980s acquisition of the largest US food companies; the 1992 USDA food pyramid with grains at its base; industry user-fees funding the majority of FDA drug review; ultra-processed foods as ~67% of US youth calories; ~90% of US health spending going to chronic and mental-health conditions; the Sackler family's extraction from Purdue and the OxyContin settlements. Group B (contested/telescoped): that Rockefeller funded medicine 'in his image' specifically to sell petroleum-derived drugs; that he lived to 97 refusing his own synthetic medicine as a homeopathy believer; the pill framed as a deliberate 'recurring revenue' scheme; that food scientists intentionally engineered addiction; the Nestle 'breast milk samples' phrasing (it was free formula samples); AAP taking $1.2M from Coca-Cola and formula-maker funding; AAP recommending GLP-1s for 12-year-olds 'to make lifelong patients'; the EU-proves-safe vs US-proves-unsafe chemical framing (real but oversimplified). Group C (asserted, no primary trace): that pharmaceutical companies 'celebrate' childhood obesity; the '77% of drug reviews' figure as stated (the real PDUFA share differs).
